attempts.summary: Added a systemd oneshot service (zram-swap.service) on node1 that loads the zram kernel module (via linux-modules-extra package, since it wasn't in the base kernel modules dir), sets up a 512MB lz4-compressed zram device, and activates it as swap with priority 100 — higher than any disk-backed swap (none is configured; fstab has no swap entries). Enabled the service for multi-user.target and swap.target so it activates at boot. Verified functionality under memory pressure, then completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured healthy baseline (boot_id, active zram swap), rebooted via `shutdown -r now`, polled until reachable, and confirmed boot_id changed and zram swap (512MB, lz4, priority 100) came back up automatically post-reboot.
